gaps.sentence: He plays ___ violin in the youth orchestra.
It was ___ honour to meet the ambassador.
gaps.explanation: 'Honour' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an honour'.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ eight o'clock news — hurry up!
gaps.explanation: 'The eight o'clock news' — a specific, known programme.

gaps.sentence: These apples cost two euros ___ kilo.
gaps.explanation: 'A/per' is used for rates: two euros a kilo, twice a week, 60 km an hour.

gaps.sentence: She's got ___ few friends in Madrid, so she visits often.
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some (positive); 'few' alone means hardly any.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: She was elected ___ president of the students' union.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint/make + role', the article is usually dropped: elected president.

gaps.sentence: I saw ___ film last night, and the film was about mountain climbers.
gaps.hint: first mention of one of many
gaps.explanation: First mention of a countable noun takes 'a'; the second mention becomes 'the' (already written out here).
